name: UNKNOT
expansion: UNsupervised K-source Number and Origin Test
tagline: How many backgrounds are there? A background-only count of sources, with a stated confidence for every answer

intro.problem: The background to a displaced-vertex search in the muon spectrometer [@atlas2014msvtx] is usually modeled as one population, yet at least three processes feed it: punch-through from collision jets, beam-induced background and cosmic muons [@atlas2016bib]. Each has its own geometry, timing and dependence on run conditions, and a single model averages over all of them.
intro.value: Knowing how many sources are present, and which events belong to each, lets every source be modeled, validated and checked for stability on its own. It also tests one mechanism behind background-estimate non-closure: two scores that are independent inside each source become dependent once the sources are mixed [@abcdisco2021].
intro.approach: UNKNOT uses background events only and lets the data set the count. Features are fitted with maximum-entropy densities [@jaynes1957]; mixtures of one to four factorized sources are scored by information criteria [@schwarz1978][@biernacki2000], subsampling and permutation tests on real events, and checked against smooth single-source alternatives. Signal simulation serves only as a geometric acceptance reference.
intro.goals: A stated confidence in the number of background sources in each detector region; a per-event membership for every source; physics checks that tie each source to an origin through jets, pileup, run stability and geometry; and a verdict on whether mixing explains the dependence between the two network scores.

questions: How many distinct background sources do the data support in each region, and with what confidence once marginal misfit and correlation within a source are controlled?
Are the candidate sources discrete populations, or one background whose shape changes smoothly with detector activity?
Does mixing sources create the dependence between the two network scores that the background estimate has to assume away?

components.name: mk1: built and run
components.subtitle: First version · background only · both regions
components.summary: The first complete version runs end to end on the current background sample in the barrel and the endcap. Every test draws its null from real events: no generated events are used anywhere, and no signal labels or training enter any number.

items.label: Health check
items.detail: Every column typed and flagged for fill values, point masses, heavy tails, dead or near-constant entries, run drift, pileup dependence and exact or affine copies; flags inform and never remove a feature

items.label: Marginals
items.detail: One-dimensional maximum-entropy fits with Legendre moment constraints, the order chosen by held-out likelihood and graded by the probability integral transform [@jaynes1957]

items.label: Source count
items.detail: Mixtures of factorized maximum-entropy sources for one to four sources, fitted by accelerated expectation-maximization [@varadhan2008] and scored three ways: information criteria, selection frequency under subsampling, and sequential permutation tests of each count against the next

items.label: Stability
items.detail: A count is accepted only where it holds as the marginals are made more flexible, and on independent halves of the runs; rigid marginals make a mixture add sources to absorb misfit

items.label: Identifiability
items.detail: Two variables give confidence in the count only; per-source shapes need three or more conditionally independent variables [@hall2003][@allman2009]

items.label: Smooth or discrete
items.detail: One source with a smooth coupling between variables, and the same models fitted within activity strata, are compared with mixtures by cross-validated likelihood, so a smooth trend is not mistaken for separate populations

items.label: Profiler
items.detail: Population or event-group comparisons across every other variable with permutation tests and false-discovery control [@bh1995], plus named checks: jet presence, pileup, run stability, event cleaning, geometry, and the score dependence inside each population

items.label: Acceptance
items.detail: Signal simulation used only as a map of where the detector reconstructs symmetric decays, so background geometry can be read against it; nothing is tuned on it

items.label: Direction
items.detail: A circular mixture fit of the missing-momentum direction relative to the vertex separates collision-aligned events from the rest without a biased chance model

components.name: mk2: per-source confidence
components.subtitle: Next version
components.summary: Three-variable sets so that each source, not only the count, carries a confidence; sources matched across resamples and run halves; evidence beyond the information-criterion approximation; and unbinned and binned cross-checks of the mixture [@benaglia2009].

links.title: Shared maximum-entropy machinery
links.text: UNKNOT reuses the same family of one-dimensional maximum-entropy fits, but asks a different question: how many sources the background contains, not how the background behaves under the ABCD assumption. Its results carry no implications for KERF.

timeline.label: Three-source background study proposed in the group: punch-through, beam-induced background and cosmic muons
Framed as background-only: suppose one to four sources and state a confidence for each; feature health check first
Named UNKNOT; maximum-entropy fits chosen over binning for every feature
mk1 built: health check, per-feature maximum-entropy fits and the source-count test; first runs in both regions
Smooth-coupling and stratified tests added; signal simulation admitted as a geometric acceptance reference only; score-provenance and profiling tools added
Missing-momentum direction model added to mk1, validated on planted toys before any real-data reading
First mk1 results summarized for internal review
Evidence for the count beyond the information-criterion approximation
Unbinned and binned cross-checks of the mixture
Physics labels assigned to sources only after the count is fixed
